observationsNotFindings: This join gets right at v1 the thing the language-runtime family needed a successor to fix. Its registerRow is the gate DR-G24 and its file08StatusToken is DR-G24's own OPEN token, with registerRowNote stating that reasoning up front rather than leaving the field to be read against the wrong row. Given that DR-131 is the substantive row in view and carries its own standing, importing that standing would have been the natural mistake.

The two-class scope is unusually well anchored. NT-1 and NT-2 are the only classes named, and that is corroborated three ways: live D-150 records that G24 owns DR-131 NT-1 and NT-2 only, the live file 08 harness cell names those two and none of NT-3 through NT-8, and the corpus phrase itself carries the parenthetical. A join that had quietly widened to the remaining NT classes would have looked like more coverage and been a scope violation.

The closure this artifact must not reopen is one it also depends on. D-150 closed NT-1 and NT-2 leftover-design with the remainder becoming G24 execution, which is precisely what makes OBL-G24-EXECUTION a qualification-at-named-gate obligation here rather than a leftover. Recording that closure as its own obligation, at leftoverDesign false, keeps the dependency visible instead of implicit.

OBL-G24-FX-AUTHORING is the single open obligation and its corpus is one phrase rather than an enumerated class list, so the remaining authoring work is less specified here than on rows like G18 or G09 where per-class exact-byte intent already exists. A later fixture cycle inherits a phrase and a two-class scope, not a member roster.
